name: archive_metadata
description: Say what protects a 7-Zip or RAR archive, structurally and through 7z, and list a ZIP; never extract. Two findings are kept apart: whether the HEADERS are encrypted (the member names need the password) and whether the members are (their data does). 7-Zip: the 32-byte start header is read from the bytes with both CRCs checked, the next header's place is checked against the file's size (an archive cut short, bytes after its end, and the first volume of a split set are named), and when the header is packed the coder list of its folder is read: 7-Zip's AES coder there means the header, and so the names, are encrypted (`protection.header_encrypted`, with its basis). Then 7z lists the members with an impossible password and no prompt (`-y`, `-spd`, a bounded run, the same lister archive_probe uses): each member's encryption flag, method and declared sizes. RAR 4 and RAR 5: every block header is read from the bytes (the RAR 4 main header's volume and password flags, the RAR 5 archive encryption header, every file header with its name, declared sizes and encrypted flag, a RAR 5 file's encryption record), each header's CRC is checked, and the chain must reach the end-of-archive block for `complete`; when the headers are encrypted the chain stops there and the member list is not available without the password (`members_listed` false, `complete`, because that is the finding). 7z is run on a RAR as a second reader where its build reads RAR (builds that drop the RAR codecs cannot, and the answer says so in `lister_note`), and a different member count is an inconsistency. ZIP: listed through 7z only, with each member's encrypted flag and method (for example AES-256); the structure of a ZIP (the central directory, the AES extra field 0x9901, data descriptors, bytes in front) is archive_probe's, from the bytes, and this tool does not read it a second time. A set of volumes: when the archive says another volume follows (a RAR end block that says so, a member continued in the next volume, a 7-Zip header past the end of the file), the next volume's name is derived from the file's name and looked for beside it (`volumes`); a missing volume makes the answer `partial` and is named. Nothing is extracted or executed: sizes are what the headers declare, and a member declared at least 1000 times larger than its packed size and 1 GiB or more is counted in `high_ratio_members_in_page` (the zip-bomb shape; the count covers the rows of the inline page) without any data being unpacked; extraction belongs to archive_extract, which has its own bounds. `complete` means the structure was read to its end, every checksum held, the set is whole and 7z, where it is needed, listed without a warning; `partial` names what was not (a CRC, a cut file, a missing volume, 7z not installed, a listing with warnings or errors, a time limit); a ZIP with no 7z answers `unavailable`. A file that is none of the three formats is `supported: false`, `partial`. The first `limit` members are inline and every member is in the JSON Lines file `all_results` names, so a RAR with a hundred thousand headers is paged, not cut. A symbolic link, a pipe, a device or a directory is refused as JSON; the file is opened without following a link and without waiting; no file the tool or 7z writes can grow past 256 MiB. Its own clock (`max_seconds`, 90 by default, at most 100) is below the manifest's timeout; it stops on SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP with one JSON answer and exit 128 + the signal, ending the 7z it started first. Withholding is by shape, measured on random draws per shape planted in a member name or path (rates, not guarantees). Printed whole in 0 of 1,000 draws: hexadecimal ids of 16, 32 and 64, numbers of 10 digits or more, recovery passwords written with dashes, spaces, dots, underscores, no separator or one to three of any other characters between the groups (an en dash, a comma, a colon, a pipe, a tab), also when the groups are cut at the separators of the path (123456-123456/123456-...), full-width, split by invisible characters, or with one decimal digit glued to the first or last group, AWS access key ids, password= and api_key: assignments, user-info, 4x4 groups of capitals and digits joined by - or ., letters and digits of 8, 9, 12, 16 or 40 characters that hold a capital, a small letter and a digit, and a full-width id. Printed whole in some draws: uniform draws of letters and digits (every character as likely a capital, a small letter or a digit as any other) of 8 characters about 2.5%, of 9 about 2%, of 12 about 1%, of 16 about 0.6%, of 24 at most 0.1% and of 40 none; random lowercase letters and digits of 8 about 7%, of 12 about 2.4%, of 16 about 0.4%; 24 random letters 1.5% to 2.6%; a 16-character base32 id 2.2% to 3.4% (by alphabet); four groups of four lowercase hexadecimal digits joined by underscores 4% to 9% (by how the draws are made); an id of 12 or 16 characters whose letters are half Cyrillic or Greek look-alikes about 1%. NOT recognised, by design, and printed whole: an identifier of 7 characters or fewer, a number of 9 digits or fewer, a lowercase-only run of up to 22 letters (it reads as a word), an all-capital letters-only run of any length, three groups of four or five capitals and digits joined by - or . (a rule for them would also withhold upper-case constants such as OpenSSL manual page names), a recovery password cut by anything other than a separator or with a letter in it or glued to it (the groups then show), a ten-digit number written 3-3-4, an e-mail-like lowercase string, and a secret of any other shape; a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true. What the rule is given is bounded: a string of more than 4096 characters (as written or after folding), a path of more than 8192, or a string with a / and a run of more than 256 name characters is withheld whole as '<text too long to judge withheld>' and not judged (the slowest string inside the bound that a search found took 0.13 CPU s). The output check, which reads every printed string once more, is narrower than the rule: with the rule removed it replaces recovery passwords (full-width ones too), AWS ids, password= values, PEM headers, user-info, hexadecimal of 16 digits or more and runs of 24 or more characters that flip between letters and digits, and it lets through numbers of 10 to 20 digits, ids of up to 23 characters, some base64 (about one in five of 32 bytes), every recovery password whose groups are joined by anything but a hyphen, underscore, dot, space or nothing, and every recovery password cut over the components of a path (the first layer alone holds those). The rule also changes names that are not secrets: of the file names of a documents tree 6.9% have a part withheld (10-digit timestamps, UUIDs) and 0.6% of its directories, of an application tree 16% and 3.1% (a word with a digit inside, such as libmp3lame, is withheld in part). A name, a path, a URL or a message that quotes a credential is withheld with the identifier-shaped strings, from version 2: a value given to a password, token, secret or cookie name (password=..., Pwd=..., a Cookie header), a Name/Value pair in text whose Name is a credential (a number, an array or a long Value too, and the NewValue after an OldValue), a -Password style switch, the argument of ConvertTo-SecureString, curl -u user:pass, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, a bcrypt hash and the known token families; the text is replaced by a marker that holds only its length. Before, only identifier-shaped strings (tokens, key ids, user-info) were withheld, so these were printed. Known gaps: a pair whose Value is an array nested in another or longer than 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, and a secret that has neither a credential name nor a token shape. It reports what 7z printed on a pipe, so a host that cannot adopt orphans does not make an answer less than complete (`program_group` says so); a process 7z leaves behind is ended and the answer is `partial`, and a process that holds 7z's pipe after 7z ended (silently, or writing without end) is let go one second after 7z ended, with the lister `listed_with_warnings` and `pipe_held`. Every answer that is not a refusal or an error carries `program_group` (subreaper, left_behind, unproven, notes).

path.description: A 7-Zip, RAR (4 or 5) or ZIP file; the first volume of a set names the missing next one. A symbolic link, device, pipe or directory is refused

limit.description: Members shown inline (default 200, 1 to 1000); every member is counted and the whole list is in the file all_results names

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 90, 1 to 100; the manifest's timeout is 120)
